rules.label: Medical Indigent Threshold #1
rules.quote: A patient whose family income is between 301% and 500% of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL). 2. Patient’s single incident medical bills are greater than 25% of yearly gross household income. 3. Patient will be billed the lesser of 5% of gross annual family income or 50% of the amounts generally billed (AGB).

rules.label: Medical Indigent Threshold #2
rules.quote: A patient whose family income is greater than 500% of the FPL. 2. Patient’s single incident Medical bills are greater than 25% of yearly gross household income. 3. Patient will be billed the lesser of 10% of gross annual family income or 50% of the AGB.

notes: Eligible services include emergency medical services, services for conditions that would lead to adverse health status if not promptly treated, non-elective services for life-threatening circumstances in non-emergency room settings, elective services excluding cosmetic procedures, and primary care services.

To qualify for financial assistance, patients must be overqualified for Hospital Discounted Care based on HDC screening or have an HDC ineligible determination letter, be financially indigent per policy criteria, be medically indigent per policy criteria, or meet presumptive eligibility based on policy criteria.

Assets considered in review include bank account balances, cash reserves, retirement/IRA balances showing withdrawals, and other easily accessible financial resources. Assets not considered include marketable assets currently listed for sale, real estate property listed for sale, tangible assets (vehicles, household goods), and non-liquid, non-convertible resources.

Financial assistance will be approved or denied based on the completed FAA and other provisions of this policy. If approved, patient accounts will be adjusted based on a sliding scale. If denied, appeals will be considered by providing additional or clarifying information for the specific denial reason listed in the letter. Assistance will retroactively cover six months from the date of approval and remain valid for one year from the first date of service applied to. Patients may reapply if six months have passed since denial, there are significant financial changes, or approved assistance is set to expire.

No account will be forwarded to collections for forty-five days after financial assistance application has been requested. A minimum of one contact attempt will be made prior to forwarding an account to collections at the guarantor level.
